steps.description:
It can be confusing when to use individual If blocks and If-Else If blocks, as they seem to produce the same results sometimes. Let's recap the difference below:

    

Their outcomes will only be the same if only one condition is true at any one time.


In the challenge, we are going to use separate If blocks to produce a fascinating program - Digital DJ Controller. It will produce quirky sounds triggered by button taps and ultrasonic sensor gestures.



We'll build it up in few parts. Using separate If blocks, create the code that checks the Ultrasonic sensor repeatedly as follows:

1. If the distance is less than 10cm, play a Tone of 500Hz for 0.1 second.

2. If the distance is less than 20cm, play a Tone of 1500Hz for 0.1 second.

3. If the distance is less than 30cm, play a Tone of 900Hz for 0.1 second.

Test out the program using virtual robot for best effect. Listen carefully, you should hear 3 sounds when the obstacle distance is less than 10cm because when it is less than 10cm, it is also less than 20cm and 30cm at the same time. So all sounds will appear one after another.

We're building a Digital DJ Controller that generates quirky sounds, triggered by button taps and ultrasonic sensor gestures.


Amend the Digital DJ Controller code from you previous step by adding a button to perform the following:

1. If Button D18 is pressed and the distance is less than 10cm, play a Tone of 500Hz for 0.1 second.

2. If Button D18 is pressed and the distance is less than 20cm, play a Tone of 1500Hz for 0.1 second.

3. If Button D18 is pressed and the distance is less than 30cm, play a Tone of 900Hz for 0.1 second.

Test out the program using virtual robot for best effect.

The Break-out-of-loop block allows you to jump out of a loop that the program is in. It must be placed inside a loop.



We're building a Digital DJ Controller that generates quirky sounds, triggered by button taps and ultrasonic sensor gestures.



Complete the Digital DJ Controller code from you previous step to perform the following:

1. If Button D18 is pressed and the distance is less than 10cm, play a Tone of 500Hz for 0.1 second.

2. If Button D18 is pressed and the distance is less than 20cm, play a Tone of 1500Hz for 0.1 second.

3. If Button D18 is pressed and the distance is less than 30cm, play a Tone of 900Hz for 0.1 second.

4. If Button D22 is pressed and the distance is less than 10cm, play a Tone  of 2000Hz for 0.1 second.

5. If Button D22 is pressed and the distance is less than 20cm, play a Tone  of 400Hz for 0.1 second.

6. If Button D22 is pressed and the distance is less than 30cm, play a Tone  of 1200Hz for 0.1 second.

7. If Button D24 is pressed break out from the loop to stop the program.

Test out the program using virtual robot for best effect but keep the volume low to avoid disturbing your peers!
